HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Furniture Words — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches furniture as a category word: not five separate facts, but one big idea — the big things that stay put — with five members of the club.

What is this?

Furniture is the family of big, unmoving things in a home: the armchair, the bookshelf, the rug, the cabinet and the stool all belong to it.

What does it mean?

Category words are a leap for young minds: sofa is a thing, furniture is a kind of thing. Once the leap lands, it lands everywhere — appliances, tools, clothes — and the world sorts itself.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and five real pieces — the card&rsquo;s five or your home&rsquo;s five. The feel-it part matters: each piece gets touched in the way that is truest to it.

Why this matters

Furniture is the gentlest category to start with: every member is big, visible and daily. Success here makes the next category word easy.

What it teaches

Category formation (member vs kind), function thinking (what is this piece FOR), and the comparison habit — how is a stool like a chair, how is it not?

Words to learn

furniturearmchairbookshelfrugcabinetstool

Say this to your child

“"Furniture is the big-word for the things that stay put. The armchair stays, the bookshelf stays — let us visit the whole family and ask each one: what is your job?"”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "all five of these belong to one family called furniture."
  2. Visit the real pieces: sit in the armchair, open and shut the cabinet once, stand on the stool beside a grown-up.
  3. Kneel on the rug — "the rug is furniture you can feel with your knees."
  4. Ask the one-job question at each piece: what does the bookshelf do? What does the stool do?
  5. Count the family: how many furniture pieces in this room?

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Furniture Words" sit over a soft blue armchair, a bookshelf with books inside, a striped rug, a two-door cabinet and a three-legged stool.

Ask your child

"Which furniture holds books?" "Which furniture do we kneel on?" "What is the difference between a chair and a stool?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might extend the family eagerly — "is the bed furniture? the dresser?" — kneel on every rug in the house to check it is real furniture, or open the cabinet to greet the dishes.

Out in the real world

Waiting rooms, schools and libraries all have furniture — the category word works the moment you walk in. Bookshelf is the member your child will meet again first.

Try it together

Furniture Says: like Simon Says, but every command is a true furniture fact — furniture says sit, furniture says kneel, furniture says open, furniture says stand on the stool with a hand. Wrong moves are giggled at, not scored.

Understanding check

Ask: "What is the big word for big stay-put things?" (furniture) "Is the sofa furniture?" (yes) "What does the bookshelf carry?" (the books)

This lesson pairs with the Furniture Words flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
